name: Italian Carbonara
description: Real carbonara has never contained cream, garlic, onion, or parsley - one Italian source puts it bluntly: add cream and 'you're not making carbonara, you're making pasta with cream and bacon.' The real, genuine creaminess comes entirely from technique - egg, cheese, rendered pork fat, and starchy pasta water emulsified together with hot pasta, off the direct heat, since eggs that get too hot simply scramble. Bacon stands in here for real guanciale or pancetta, missing their real, less-smoky depth.

ingredients_full.note: cubed, standing in for guanciale or pancetta
finely grated, standing in for pecorino romano

ingredients.note: cubed, standing in for guanciale or pancetta

steps_detailed: Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente, reserving a cup of the starchy pasta water before draining.
Cook the bacon in a cold pan over medium heat until the fat renders and it turns crisp.
Whisk the egg yolks with the cheese and black pepper, being generous with the pepper.
Off the heat, toss the hot, drained pasta with the bacon and its rendered fat.

Add the egg-cheese mixture and toss vigorously off the heat, adding splashes of the reserved pasta water until glossy and creamy - real technique never returns the pan to direct heat here, or the eggs will scramble instead of emulsifying.

name: Italian Bolognese
description: Ragù alla bolognese, a real slow-simmered meat sauce, genuinely depends on patience - real technique starts with a soffritto of onion, carrot, and celery cooked down thoroughly, then the meat browned deeply, and the sauce simmered low for hours, with a splash of milk stirred in near the end for real richness.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and carrot together, 8-10 minutes, until well softened - this real soffritto is the base of the sauce.
Add the beef and brown deeply, 8-9 minutes.
Add the wine and let it fully reduce, 2-3 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and diced tomatoes, and simmer, uncovered, at least 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the milk in the last 10 minutes for real richness.

description: A simple, bright tomato sauce echoing the flavors of pizza margherita, real technique keeping the ingredients minimal so the tomato's own real flavor carries the sauce.

Add the tomatoes and simmer 15-18 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the torn basil off the heat, just before serving.

name: Italian Risotto
description: Risotto depends genuinely on real technique - the rice is toasted dry first, then broth is added gradually, one ladle at a time, stirred constantly, which is what releases the rice's natural starch and builds the real creamy texture.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in half the butter, 3-4 minutes.
Add the rice and toast, stirring, 2 minutes, without letting it brown.
Add the warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to mostly absorb before adding the next, 18-20 minutes total.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter and the cheese for a final real creamy finish.
